papers.title: Cell-state conditioning predicts the expression response to an unseen stimulus but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects
papers.abstract: Second-generation sequence models can be conditioned on a cell state supplied as a single-cell snapshot rather than selected from a fixed catalogue, but whether that conditioning carries an experimentally applied perturbation has not been tested. We conditioned such a model on interferon-{beta}-stimulated and unstimulated monocytes from a published experiment, using cells disjoint from those providing the measurement, and asked whether the predicted expression response tracks the measured one and whether the same conditioning identifies expression QTL specific to the stimulated state. Predicted and measured responses agree at Spearman {rho} = 0.616 across 119 genes (95% CI 0.486 to 0.716), and at 0.607 after all 119 target genes are deleted from the conditioning input; across fifteen conditions the model's response scales with how much each condition's biology genuinely overlaps the target response (slope 0.73, Pearson 0.92), and a near-neighbour monocyte subset receives 0.295 against a measured overlap of 0.336. For stimulation-specific genetic effects we find no reliable evidence: the pre-specified primary arm moves from p = 0.0019 to 0.443 once both conditions must carry a measurable predicted effect, and the separation localises to the resting-condition baseline. Neither model generation's catalogue contains a perturbed sample, 0 of 4,430 tracks and 0 of 2,799 conditions, although both carry activation-state labels, so the gap is experimental perturbation rather than cell state. Two incidental findings apply beyond this model: credible-set membership mislabels over half of putatively condition-specific loci, and gating a ratio statistic on its larger term manufactures signal.

papers.title: KORUS: probabilistic ancestry inference beyond variant calls
papers.abstract: Ancestry inference typically relies on variant calling and predefined population labels. We present KORUS, a probabilistic framework that infers ancestry from sequencing-derived k-mer representations constructed using ancestry-informative reference variants and encoded in Bloom filters, without requiring explicit variant calls for query genomes. KORUS separates genomic feature representation from ancestry decoding, enabling supervised classification, fractional ancestry inference, and unsupervised population structure discovery within a unified framework. Reference models were constructed from 643 genomes from the 1000 Genomes Project and the Simons Genome Diversity Project. Evaluation on an independent cohort of 22 whole-genome sequencing samples, with comparisons to ntRoot, SNVstory, and ADMIXTURE, showed recovery of continental-scale population structure, with supervised classification accuracy of 72.7-81.8% and ancestry-fraction concordance of R2 = 0.844-0.993 relative to ADMIXTURE and R2 = 0.665-0.983 relative to ntRoot. Ancestry estimates were consistent across alternative k-mer representations. Analyses of ancient human and archaic hominin genomes demonstrated that probabilistic projections quantify affinity to the learned feature space rather than necessarily indicating modern continental ancestry. KORUS provides a unified approach to ancestry inference directly from sequencing-derived representations and is freely available under the GPLv3 license at https://github.com/BirolLab/korus.

papers.title: The pangenome of the Arctic picoeukaryote Micromonas polaris resolves cryptic ecotypes and identifies a polar-specific gene repertoire
papers.abstract: Micromonas polaris is the dominant picoeukaryote of the Arctic Ocean, where it sustains primary production across habitats from sea ice to open water to the subsurface chlorophyll maximum. How a single species maintains this ecological breadth has remained unclear. Standard phylogenetic markers such as 18S rRNA are nearly invariant within M. polaris and conceal any internal genomic heterogeneity the species may possess. Here we present a pangenome of 14 M. polaris strains spanning the Arctic basin, integrated with Tara Oceans metagenomes, that resolves the species into two diverged ecotypes invisible to 18S rRNA but recovered consistently by prp8, genome-wide SNPs, ANI, and orthogroup-based phylogenies. The two ecotypes coexist sympatrically, with one lineage consistently enriched deeper in the water column across the basin. M. polaris carries 990 polar-specific hierarchical orthogroups absent from temperate Micromonas, organised around one-carbon metabolism, endocytosis, transmembrane transport, and photo-oxidative stress response. Several components show phylogenetic signatures of horizontal acquisition from co-occurring marine taxa. Atlantification is bringing temperate Micromonas into Arctic margins seasonally, but the polar night likely limits their year-round persistence. M. polaris and its polar-specific toolkit appear positioned to persist through the dark season, suggesting Arctic margins will undergo seasonal turnover rather than stable replacement.

papers.title: Vertical transmission and community turnover in seed-borne microbiomes: lessons from an aMAIZEing model system
papers.abstract: The seed microbiome represents a specialized ecological niche, governed by assembly processes that are only partially coupled to the surrounding soil community. While environmental recruitment and vertical transmission from the maternal plant are both recognized sources of seed-associated microorganisms, the mechanisms that determine their relative contributions and whether these contributions shift across generations remain poorly understood. Here, we used long-read metagenomic sequencing to track seed-borne bacterial community dynamics across a founding seed pool and two subsequent generations in two divergent maize (Zea mays L.) varieties exposed to contrasting organic and mineral fertilisation regimes. We recovered 112 medium- or high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes and combined MAG-level taxonomic and functional analyses with genus-level community profiling to characterize persistence and turnover dynamics within the seed microbiome. While soil taxonomic diversity was high, seed-associated communities showed a near-complete compositional disconnect from soil-dominant assemblages taxa, with a persistent Firmicutes core maintained across generations, consistent with vertical transmission. Priority effects remain a possible explanation for these patterns but were not directly tested. Genus-level source attribution suggested greater environmental recruitment under organic fertilization, with more diverse soil communities and a stronger contribution from the preceding seed generation under mineral fertilization. Seed-associated MAGs also carried genes associated with plant growth-promoting potential, although these detections could not be consistently linked to specific transmission routes. In contrast, maize genotype had no detectable effect on seed microbiome composition. Intergenerational persistence and environmental recruitment jointly shape seed-derived communities under contrasting fertilization regimes. Their relative contributions remain inferred from taxonomic overlap, and the effects of microbial source-pool diversity cannot be separated from the accompanying differences in soil chemistry in this design.

papers.title: Genetic regulation of ALK inhibitor response in diverse human cell types
papers.abstract: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) inhibitors are effective treatments for ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer but cause diverse adverse events affecting multiple tissues. Genetic variation may contribute to inter-individual differences in susceptibility, but the small number of treated patients limits the power of genetic association studies. Moreover, the diversity of affected tissues and cell types makes functional investigation challenging. We used induced pluripotent stem cells from 49 individuals to generate heterogeneous differentiating cultures (HDCs) containing multiple cell types, treated them with five ALK inhibitors (crizotinib, alectinib, ceritinib, brigatinib, and lorlatinib) for 24 hours, and characterized transcriptional responses using single-cell RNA sequencing. These responses showed cell-type-specific and shared transcriptional effects. Integrating gene expression with individual genotypes, we identified 4,371 expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) across 21 cell types, including 2,137 response eQTLs whose regulatory effects differ between untreated and drug-treated cells. These results nominate candidates for future studies of ALK inhibitor toxicity.

papers.title: Pharmacological and genetic access to astrocytic cholesterol programs in human neural cells
papers.abstract: Astrocyte-neuron interactions coordinate cholesterol metabolism, cell adhesion, and synaptic gene expression1,2, and related gene expression programs decline together in schizophrenia3. Whether pharmacological or genetic perturbations can selectively engage components of this coordinated biology was unknown. Here we combine genetically diverse cultures of human stem-cell-derived neurons and astrocytes, pharmacological profiling, genetic association mapping and CRISPR interference to examine these biological programs. In stem-cell-derived astrocyte mono-cultures, the antipsychotic clozapine induced a focused transcriptional response involving cholesterol biosynthesis and export, and drove an increase in intracellular and secreted cholesterol. This response overlapped with the cholesterol-related component of the astrocytic response to neuronal contact seen in neuron-astrocyte co-cultures, but did not extend to synaptic cell-adhesion genes. In neuron-astrocyte co-cultures, clozapine also increased neuronal firing. Across individual cell donors, cholesterol-pathway induction by clozapine was broadly shared but varied in magnitude. Gene-expression patterns in untreated donors were associated with differential responses to clozapine and the liver X receptor agonist GW3965. Common genetic variation influenced expression of several cholesterol-related genes, including a clozapine-dependent association of HSD17B7 expression with nearby genetic variants. Independently, repression of LDLR induced coordinated expression of cholesterol-biosynthesis genes in astrocytes that overlapped with astrocyte responses to clozapine and neuronal contact. These findings identify shared cholesterol-related transcriptional responses to pharmacological and genetic perturbations and link common genetic variation to distinct features of cholesterol-pathway responses.

papers.title: Air and environmental sampling expand metagenomic viral surveillance in Cambodian pig slaughterhouses
papers.abstract: Surveillance of viruses in swine depends largely on the sampling of individual animals chosen at random, often limiting detection breadth. Environmental sampling has emerged as an alternative strategy, enabling faster, safer and more cost-effective pathogen monitoring at the human-animal interfaces. Across nine visits to two Cambodian slaughterhouses, we applied metagenomic sequencing to air samples (n = 25), faeces (n = 156), wastewater (n = 15), carcass wash water (n = 18), holding-pen swabs (n = 124), slaughter-box swabs (n = 73) and ropes (n = 16), comparing virus composition to pig snout swabs (n = 193). Combined environmental sampling recovered 96.6% of the viral taxa detected in snout swabs, exceeding 90.9% at every visit. Greater viral diversity was consistently captured in the environment, including swine-associated taxa absent from snout swabs and viral RNA associated with avian and human hosts. Air provided the widest coverage of any single environmental sample type and contributed the largest number of independent virus detections that were not recovered from any other environmental sample. Slaughter-box swabs recovered the fewest taxa, showing that visible contamination with swine material did not correlate with greater viral recovery. Overall, this study identifies air as a pivotal core component of any surveillance program. However, pairing air with additional environmental sample types provides the broadest virus coverage and represents the optimal surveillance strategy in swine slaughterhouses.

papers.title: Brain disorder mechanisms and therapeutic targets identified from developmental, cell-specific gene regulation
papers.abstract: Genetic variation influences brain physiology and disease across cell types and development. We integrated whole-genome sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, and single-nucleus multiome profiling from 231 human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex donors spanning six postconceptional weeks to 92 years. Across 24 brain-related traits, neurodevelopmental and psychiatric genetic risk was enriched in neuronal transcriptomic and chromatin profiles, whereas neurodegenerative risk was enriched in microglia. Thousands of expression, chromatin accessibility, and splicing quantitative trait loci revealed developmental and cell-type-specific regulatory effects. Colocalization linked multiple sclerosis risk to AHI1 expression in prenatal neurons and problematic alcohol use to GPX1 expression in postnatal glia. Leveraging dynamic cis-regulatory elements, we identified therapeutic candidates for haploinsufficient neurodevelopmental disorders, including a SOX5 enhancer whose CRISPR activation increased transcript and protein abundance. Together, these findings establish a publicly accessible genomic resource for resolving the developmental and cellular contexts of genetic risk and identifying therapeutic targets in the human brain.

papers.title: A full-length isoform atlas of the non-failing and failing human heart
papers.abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and ischemic heart disease (IHD) are leading causes of heart failure, yet isoform-level changes in the failing heart remain poorly defined because reference annotations are derived largely from healthy tissues and short-read sequencing cannot reliably reconstruct full-length transcripts. We sequenced six human left ventricles (non-failing, DCM, and IHD; n = 2 each) with PacBio HiFi long reads and curated 48,232 isoforms across 11,760 genes, including 15,535 novel NIC and NNC isoforms. Independent evidence supported most novel structures: 81.7% of isoforms with novel splice junctions had short-read support for all novel junctions, and a cardiac CAGE atlas supported the 5' ends of 93% of NIC and 86% of NNC isoforms. Novel isoform diversification was concentrated in sarcomere genes and persisted after accounting for gene complexity, expression, sequencing depth, and transcript length. We then augmented GENCODE v43 with 18,637 non-FSM long-read isoforms and re-quantified two independent short-read cohorts (MAGNet and GSE116250). For most genes carrying a transcript that changed more than 2-fold in DCM, the gene itself changed less than 2-fold, so these changes are not apparent at the gene level. Of 626 transcripts differentially expressed in both cohorts, 98% changed in the same direction, including all 100 long-read isoforms among them. The resource is available through CardioIsoMap, an interactive isoform-centric portal (https://cardioisomap.streamlit.app/). This study provides a comprehensive isoform-resolved reference of the human heart in health and disease.

papers.title: CTCF-anchored cohesin loops are a vertebrate-specific innovation
papers.abstract: Animal genomes are organized into chromatin loops and topologically associating domains. Cohesin drives loop extrusion, and the architectural factor CTCF halts loop-extruding cohesin. CTCF-anchored loops facilitate interactions between distal cis-regulatory elements and regulate gene expression. However, when CTCF acquired its cohesin loop-halting function remains unclear. We performed interspecies domain-swap experiments, replacing the cohesin-interacting N-terminus of mouse CTCF with orthologous sequences from the fruit fly Drosophila (arthropod), Branchiostoma (chordate), and the inshore hagfish (jawless vertebrate). The hagfish N-terminus halted cohesin, whereas the invertebrate CTCF N-termini did not. Consistently, Micro-C maps from hagfish tissues revealed stripes associated with convergently oriented CTCF sites, a characteristic signature of cohesin-loop halting. Notably, cohesin enrichment at promoters and enhancers was more pronounced in hagfish than in jawed vertebrates. Our findings indicate that CTCF-mediated cohesin loop anchoring most likely evolved in the common ancestor of extant vertebrates and was further strengthened in jawed vertebrates.

papers.title: Pluripotent and differentiated cells display distinct genomic and nuclear landscapes of genome folding variability
papers.abstract: Chromosome folding varies between cells. It is not known whether cell types differ in the extent of folding variability, whether distinct chromosomal regions in the same cell type display different levels of variability, and how folding variability relates to sub-nuclear location and gene expression. We combined two single-cell Hi-C approaches with 3D genome modeling of pseudo-single cells (IGM), DNA FISH, chromosome painting, and single-cell RNA-seq across a five-stage differentiation trajectory from human embryonic stem cells to hepatocyte-like cells. In all cell types folding variability correlates with compartment status, is highest towards the nuclear interior, decreases as a function of radial position in the nucleus, and is the lowest at the periphery. Loci associated with nuclear landmarks such as speckles, and especially the nuclear periphery display more consistent subnuclear positioning in all cell stages. Moreover, pluripotent and differentiated cells display different overall levels of chromosome folding variability: in H1 pluripotent cells the entire genome displays higher folding and positional variability. In contrast, in differentiated cells folding variability is generally lower along the genome and the number of loci that become consistently positioned at the nuclear periphery increases sharply. The two distinct patterns of folding variability were correlated with cell-to-cell gene expression variation: In pluripotent cells gene expression variation is large, pervasive and seen throughout the genome and the nucleus. In differentiated cells cell-to-cell variation in gene expression is much lower and restricted mostly to genes located near the center of the nucleus, consistent with the restricted pattern of chromosome folding variation. These findings reveal two distinct genomic states: pluripotent cells maintain a variably folded, spatially permissive genome and transcriptional plasticity, whereas differentiated cells mature into a spatially deterministic, more consistently folded organization that correlates with more restricted transcriptional programs.

papers.title: Genome architecture and duplication-associated functional diversification in the carnivorous plant Sarracenia purpurea
papers.abstract: The repeated evolution of complex traits raises the question of how genomes generate ecological novelty while preserving developmental organization. We present a chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation for the carnivorous purple pitcher plant, Sarracenia purpurea, and investigate how two contrasting modes of gene duplication have shaped its genome and functional repertoire: ancient polyploidy, which leaves duplicated genes in conserved chromosomal regions (syntenic duplicates), and local tandem duplication, which generates neighboring gene copies. We compare these duplication classes across nine angiosperms. The genome shows a mosaic of conserved and fractionated duplicated regions reflecting differential retention and loss of genes following ancient polyploidy and later restructuring. Comparison with noncarnivorous Actinidia (kiwifruit) identifies 18 syntenic and nine tandem Gene Ontology (GO) Biological Process term-duplication-class combinations enriched in Sarracenia but not significantly enriched in Actinidia. Syntenic enrichments include meristem maintenance, organ-boundary specification, cuticle development, and hormonal regulation; tandem enrichments include defense responses, oxidative stress, jasmonic-acid biosynthesis, leaf senescence, and oligopeptide transport. Across the carnivorous genera Sarracenia, Nepenthes, Utricularia, and Pinguicula, we identify 19 syntenic and two tandem-associated biological processes showing significant enrichment in all four lineages, revealing striking functional commonalities across multiple evolutionary origins of carnivory despite their divergent trap morphologies and ecological strategies. Among Sarracenia genes differentially expressed in at least one comparison of flower, pitcher-leaf, and root tissues, tandem-class genes exhibit larger maximum absolute expression differences and greater GO richness and effective breadth at matched numbers of annotated homologs. These results highlight the complementary evolutionary contributions of ancient genome duplication and local gene-family expansion to the developmental and ecological diversification of carnivorous plants.

papers.title: Efficient genome graphs indexing, querying and visualization with gfaidx and gfaidx-viz
papers.abstract: Genome graphs enable the analysis of genetic variation across many genomes, but exploring individual regions remains computationally demanding. We present gfaidx, a general-purpose indexer giving fast, low-memory access to pangenome, assembly, and de Bruijn graphs in GFA format. It retrieves gene-sized subgraphs and their haplotypes over 100-fold faster than existing tools such as ODGI and vg, and can index human pangenome-scale graphs on a personal computer. The accompanying gfaidx-viz interactively visualizes pre-indexed human pangenomes. Both are freely available at https://github.com/fawaz-dabbaghieh/gfaidx and https://github.com/fawaz-dabbaghieh/gfaidx-viz

papers.title: A spatial correlation function approach reveals zonation loss in liver disease
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics measures the expression of hundreds to thousands of genes in each cell together with the cell's position in the tissue. Here we use spatial correlation functions, which describe how the correlation of gene expression between cells decays with distance, to quantify how the spatial organization of gene expression changes in disease. From the correlation function of each gene, or of each pair of genes, we extract two numbers: a susceptibility, which measures how strongly gene expression is correlated between nearby cells, and a correlation length, the distance over which this correlation extends. Both are in physical units and can be compared directly between samples and conditions. We apply the approach to healthy and fibrotic mouse liver using newly generated data, and to healthy and fibrotic human liver using published data. Correlations between gene pairs identify genes of the same hepatocyte zone, and assign a zone to 1,266 genes that are not known zonation markers. The two fibrotic conditions differ: CCl4 injection in mice produces a moderate reorganization in which some genes lose spatial correlation and others gain it, while in human fibrosis almost every measured gene loses it. Changes in spatial correlation are only weakly related to changes in expression level. For instance Cyp2c29 and Pon1 partially lose their spatial correlation in treated mice, although their average expression does not consistently fall. Spatial correlation functions therefore detect changes in tissue organization that measurements of expression level alone miss.

papers.title: Deciphering the genetic bases of canine longevity
papers.abstract: Across dog breeds, the inverse correlation between body size and lifespan is well documented, but its genetic basis remains poorly understood, in part because size and lifespan are confounded at the breed level. Here, we assembled the Cani-DNA discovery cohort of 540 dogs from 27 breeds, with 20 dogs per breed, genotyped by low-pass whole-genome sequencing and imputation. We performed genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of breed-average body weight, breed-median lifespan and individual age at death, and tested the age-at-death loci for replication in the GRLS replication cohort of 3,024 Golden Retrievers. The GWAS of breed-average body weight recovered established body-size loci, confirming that the cohort could detect known associations. Of the 69 breed-weight loci, 30 were shared with breed-median lifespan, and at all of them the allele increasing body weight was associated with shorter lifespan. At the individual level, age at death, with breed-average body weight as a covariate, identified loci distinct from all breed-level loci. Three of them, the CDH4, TSHZ3 and TSC22D2 loci, replicated in the GRLS replication cohort. In humans, CDH4 and TSHZ3 have been implicated in longevity, and the region orthologous to the TSC22D2 locus has been associated with markers of biological ageing. Together, these results identify genetic variation associated with the lifespan of individual dogs beyond breed body size, and support the dog as a model in which genetic leads on ageing can be identified.

papers.title: Expanding the human T cell receptor germline reference through population-scale pangenome analysis using the gAIRR Suite version 2
papers.abstract: The germline gene set encoding the adaptive immune receptor repertoire (gAIRR) defines the allele space from which the expressed repertoire (exprAIRR) is assembled, so an incomplete gAIRR reference propagates errors into T cell receptor (TR) annotation and genotyping and is also a barrier to studying inherited TR variation in its own right. Human TR gAIRR diversity remains incompletely characterized because the loci resist short-read resolution and because locus-resolved cohorts have been small. We developed gAIRR Suite version 2, in which each gAIRR-annotate query carries 50 bp of germline sequence on either side of the allele core and a call is reported only when the assembly supports the core together with both flanks, and in which gAIRR-call genotypes from Element AVITI libraries whose 500-bp Read 1 spans a complete V core with its flanking anchors. Applying this framework to Human Pangenome Reference Consortium Release 2 (464 haplotype-resolved assemblies from 232 individuals across five superpopulations), we identified 531 novel TR alleles (486 TRV, 45 TRJ), each observed in the targeted-sequencing reads of at least one carrier, of which 298 were absent from our 47-individual Release 1 catalogue. In 216 individuals, targeted genotyping with gAIRR-seq and gAIRR-call recovered 99.985% of the 61,628 evaluated alleles found in the corresponding assemblies, with a precision of 99.995%. Release 2 added few common alleles but many rare ones: 407 of the 531 were restricted to a single superpopulation, and African-ancestry individuals accounted for 51.1% of these (46.0% {+/-} 2.1% after downsampling to equal group size) while comprising 30.2% of the cohort. Population-scale pangenome analysis therefore extends the TR gAIRR reference chiefly by recovering variation that smaller or less diverse cohorts would miss.

papers.title: Learning gene co-regulation across cells with Multicellular Transformer
papers.abstract: Understanding how genes coordinate across cells is central to explaining tissue function and disease, yet most existing models still take a single cell as input and therefore emphasize cell-intrinsic regulation. We present the Multicellular Transformer (MCT), a foundation model built around a different assumption: cells function together within tissues, so the appropriate unit of input is not one cell in isolation but a set of cells from the same sample. By jointly modeling multiple cells, MCT learns context-aware gene embeddings that capture gene-gene interactions across the tissue environment. Trained on a large set of tissue samples (>4200) across more than 30 tissue types, MCT recovers ligand-receptor interactions, infers cross-cell signaling programs, and reveals spatial co-localization patterns directly from scRNA-seq data. Its contextual embeddings identify disease-specific rewiring of gene neighborhoods in systemic lupus erythematosus and COVID-19 and predict population-level perturbation effects in cancer without additional training. By linking gene-level regulation to tissue-scale organization, MCT provides a scalable framework for modeling multicellular biology and enables in silico discovery of therapeutic targets and tissue-specific dependencies.

papers.title: GRASER: haplotype assignment of graph-aligned short reads
papers.abstract: Existing read phasing tools operate on reads aligned to a linear reference, where reference bias reduces the information available for haplotype inference and read assignment. Pangenome graphs reduce reference bias, but reads falling within non-reference sequence cannot be surjected to a linear reference, so phasing after surjection reintroduces that bias. Here we present GRASER, which phases graph-aligned short reads against haplotype paths inferred for each individual, using established graph genotyping and statistical phasing to build those paths. GRASER phase uses edges unique to one haplotype path as evidence, so reads are phased directly from graph alignments without conversion to a linear reference. Against true parental haplotype paths, GRASER assigned 22.6 to 24.5% of simulated fragments to a haplotype, and more than 96% of those were placed on the correct haplotype. Inferred haplotype paths reduced the assignment rate by about 4 percentage points. GRASER assigned more fragments than a WhatsHap-based linear-reference workflow in every configuration tested. Applied to whole-genome bisulfite sequencing, GRASER recovered allele-specific methylation at imprinted loci and measured haplotype-resolved methylation within a structural variant.

papers.title: Midkine and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: evidence from Mendelian randomization, multi-omics factor analysis, and single-cell transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most lethal malignancies, in part because its tumor microenvironment actively suppresses antitumor immunity. Midkine (MDK) is a secreted heparin-binding growth factor that is overexpressed in a majority of PDAC tumors, but whether it contributes causally to disease risk and through which cell types it acts have not been firmly established. We combined cis-eQTL Mendelian randomization (GTEx pancreas, n = 328 donors; FinnGen PDAC, 1,252 cases) with multi-omics factor analysis (MOFA) of TCGA-PAAD tumors (n = 149), single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA), cross-species single-cell RNA sequencing, and DepMap CRISPR dependency screening. Mendelian randomization identified MDK as the only gene passing false discovery rate correction for PDAC risk (inverse-variance-weighted odds ratio 1.51, 95% CI 1.19-1.91, p = 6.7 x 10??; FDR = 0.008), with concordant direction across five methods and five independent GWAS. MDK was overexpressed in tumors relative to adjacent normal tissue in an independent cohort (GSE62452, n = 130, p = 5 x 10??), and high expression was associated with shorter overall survival (10.2 versus 21.1 months, p = 0.023). In the MOFA decomposition, MDK localized to a factor characterized by tertiary lymphoid structure gene expression but negative correlation with dendritic cells and macrophages, a pattern consistent with immune exclusion. Single-cell analysis and published functional studies indicated that MDK is produced by cancer-associated fibroblasts and endothelial cells rather than by tumor epithelium, and DepMap data confirmed that MDK is not a cell-autonomous fitness gene. Collectively, these results support a model in which MDK acts through the stromal-immune compartment rather than through tumor cell-intrinsic mechanisms, and raise the possibility that MDK blockade could restore antitumor immunity in PDAC.

papers.title: Somatic mutation probabilities learned from the DNA sequence
papers.abstract: Somatic mutations distribute heterogeneously over genomes, dependent on immediate sequence context, function, and non-genetic factors. Mutations present the foundation for somatic genome evolution towards age-related diseases. Here, we present EAGLE-MUT, a group of DNA language models trained on sparse single base substitution data from esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) and melanoma (MELA) samples. In both cancer types, predicted mutation probabilities vary across several orders of magnitude, depending on sequence context. For example, T>G hotspots in EAC localize to A/T-rich ~200 base pair DNA motifs, associated with nucleosome positioning. Coldspots localize to G/C-rich DNA, nucleosome linker DNA, CTCF binding sites, potential origins of replication, and intron-exon boundaries with a transcription strand bias. Fine-tuning EAGLE-MUT for individual patient samples leads to varying mutation distributions relative to genome elements and potential cancer driver mutations. EAGLE-MUT provides new links between DNA sequence, genome function, and stability in individual samples, a foundation for understanding somatic genome evolution, and more personalized strategies for risk-assessment, prevention, and treatment.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics mapping of human ovarian aging across young and menopausal transition
papers.abstract: Ovarian aging is an early feature of human aging with broad consequences for women's health, yet its cellular dynamics across the menopausal transition remain unclear. We integrated single-cell transcriptomic, chromatin accessibility and spatial transcriptomic profiles across young, menopausal-transition and postmenopausal human ovaries. Granulosa cells (GCs) exhibited the most pronounced age-associated transcriptional remodelling. The menopausal transition was characterized by reduced DNA-repair activity and elevated stress-response programs in GCs, alongside broader changes in hormone-response and steroid-metabolic programs during ovarian aging. Integrated regulatory analyses implicated HEYL, a GC-enriched transcription factor, with reduced accessibility at a putative regulatory element during aging. Genetic analyses associated HEYL and its predicted upstream regulators with age at natural menopause, while spatial mapping revealed enrichment of menopause-associated genetic signals in GC-rich regions. HEYL depletion increased senescence-associated phenotypes in human granulosa-like cells and primary mouse GCs, whereas overexpression attenuated oxidative-stress-induced senescence. Perturbation of its orthologue Hey produced consistent effects in Drosophila ovaries. Together, our atlas reveals stage-associated granulosa-cell remodeling and implicates HEYL in ovarian aging.

papers.title: Identification of JMJD1C as a key mediator of fibroblast remodelling in human AF by single-nucleus multi-omics
papers.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent arrhythmia, accounting for up to 15% of arrhythmias in the elderly. Atrial enlargement associated with fibrotic and hypertrophic remodelling, termed atrial myopathy (AM), is considered a precursor to AF development. The mechanisms underlying the development of AM and its progression to AF remain incompletely resolved. To identify the unique and combined contributions of the major cellular mediators of AM and AF, we combine single-nucleus transcriptomics of human left and right atrial appendages (LAA and RAA) with paired RNA and chromatin-accessibility profiling of 20 LAA samples. We validate these findings through histological and functional studies in primary human cardiac fibroblasts (HCFs). Patients were stratified according to the presence of AF and AM (identified by left atrial volume dimensions; LAVI, Hi and Lo), generating Hi-AF, Hi-SR, Lo-AF and Lo-SR groups that separate AF-associated from structural-remodelling-associated alterations. Across 75,654 qualified nuclei, AF was associated with chamber-dependent shifts in cellular composition and gene expression, with extracellular matrix (ECM) and TGF-beta programmes prominent in LAA. Multiome analysis identified a stressed atrial cardiomyocyte (aCM4) state expressing natriuretic peptide A (NPPA) and natriuretic peptide B (NPPB), with altered cis-regulatory connectivity, and an inflammatory fibroblast (PTGDS+ FB) state characterised by IL-6 expression and matrix- and TGF-beta-associated programmes. Enhancer-driven network analysis identified GLIS3, TWIST2 and TBX20 as regulators of FB state transitions. The histone demethylase JMJD1C was enriched in PTGDS+ FB and induced by TGF-beta; its depletion attenuated alpha-smooth-muscle-actin (alpha-SMA) accumulation and reprogrammed TGF-beta-responsive transcription. Ligand-receptor analysis further predicted macrophage-to-FB TGF-beta signalling, showing the contribution of macrophages to the atrial inflammatory environment. These data define discrete aspects of rhythm- and structure-associated remodelling of human atrial tissue and identify a candidate macrophage-TGF-beta-JMJD1C-FB interaction for potential therapeutic development.

papers.title: Cell atlases of schistosome human infective stages reveal larval tissue fates and innovations
papers.abstract: Schistosomes infect over 250 million people, yet the cellular basis of their human-infective cercaria larva, that drives transmission and infection, remains poorly understood. We present single-cell atlases of Schistosoma mansoni cercariae, widely regarded as transcriptionally quiescent, and schistosomula, the first intra-mammalian stage. Twenty-two cercarial cell types either persist into schistosomula or are lost. The tail harbours several cercaria-specific innovations, including a novel tegument. Gene-age analysis supports the cercaria as the most recent addition to the life cycle and tail cells as younger than body cells. Persisting cell types undergo clear transcriptional transitions which give new insights into the dynamics of cercarial transformation into schistosomula. These findings link the recent origin of cercarial cell types to the evolution of active dispersal and transmission in digenean parasites.

papers.title: Improved long-read sequencing technology reveals full genome architecture of Malian Plasmodium falciparum field isolates
papers.abstract: Understanding genome plasticity in malaria parasites and the diversity of their repetitive gene families requires high-quality reference genomes derived from parasites recently isolated from patients. However, generating such genomes in Plasmodium falciparum remains challenging owing to the parasite's extreme AT content, extensive repetitive regions, and the frequent occurrence of multiclonal infections in endemic settings. As a result, most available reference genomes are derived from laboratory-adapted strains, that have experienced prolonged in vitro maintenance, and that incompletely represent natural parasite diversity. We developed and optimized a de novo assembly strategy based on PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and applied it to eight recently-isolated and cloned P. falciparum parasites from Mali. HiFi sequencing enabled highly accurate genome reconstruction, yielding assemblies with a mean of 18 contigs, 301 pseudogenes, and a frameshift rate of 0.04% following Liftoff annotation. Assemblies showed high structural integrity and near-complete chromosomes, including improved recovery of subtelomeric regions and multigene families, without requiring short-read correction. Despite overall conservation of chromosome organization, substantial variation was observed in chromosome-end architecture, subtelomeric structure, and telomeric repeat content among parasite genomes. Our approach simplifies the generation of high-quality P. falciparum genomes and reduces sequencing requirements fourfold. The resulting assemblies enabled characterization of natural variation in telomere plasticity and multicopy gene family diversity in field isolates. These findings establish PacBio HiFi sequencing as an effective and scalable strategy for producing highly contiguous and accurate de novo assemblies of P. falciparum, supporting the development of geographically-diverse, field-relevant malaria parasite reference genomes.

papers.title: A genome-guided multilocus sequence analysis scheme to detect and resolve diversity within the X-disease phytoplasma group (16SrIII)
papers.abstract: Phytoplasmas of the X-disease group (16SrIII) cause economically important diseases of vegetables, forage and staple crops, fruit trees and ornamentals in South America, where they are diagnosed and classified only by 16S rRNA gene RFLP. Because this gene is highly conserved, strains that differ in host range, vectors and regulatory relevance cannot be distinguished. We developed a multilocus sequence analysis (MLSA) scheme for typing 16SrIII phytoplasmas, using genome data to select the markers and to define reference lineages. Five single-copy loci (tuf, secA, secY, mutM, cimH) were chosen from 16 curated genomes; primers matched all genomes in silico, and four of the five pairs did not amplify phytoplasmas of other groups co-occurring in the region (16SrI, 16SrVII, 16SrXIII). Genome comparisons resolved four lineages, including one restricted to South America that shared only 90.8-93.9% average nucleotide identity with the other lineages, despite > 98.8% 16S rRNA identity. The concatenated MLSA (2,870 nt) reproduced the genome-based lineages and assigned five Argentinian field isolates from weeds, fodder beet, cassava, plum and a native shrub. Identical 16SrIII-B RFLP patterns occurred in different lineages, and one 16SrIII-B isolate grouped within the 16SrIII-J clade, showing that subgroups are not reliable proxies for lineages. The South American lineage had the broadest host range, spanning six plant families. We also detected chimeric rRNA copies and sequencing artefacts that can cause misclassification. This MLSA provides a PCR-based tool to identify 16SrIII lineages in crops, weeds and insects, supporting epidemiological studies, disease management and phytosanitary decisions.

papers.title: Single-cell transfer RNA sequencing reveals principles of translational regulation
papers.abstract: Transfer RNAs (tRNAs) decode genetic instructions from messenger RNA (mRNA) into protein, yet their abundance and regulation across cell states remain largely undefined, as multimodal measures of cellular tRNAs have remained elusive. Here, we develop a massively parallel assay for single-cell translatome and RNA sequencing (sctRNA-seq), which profiles transcriptome-wide mRNA and tRNA abundance simultaneously and chart the tRNA composition of 364,841 cells. Through multimodal perturbation screening of protein-coding genes and tRNA loci, we reveal dynamics across the mRNA and tRNA transcriptomes, delineating distinct tRNA-linked modules regulated by metabolic and Pol III-mediated transcription. Further, we uncover a close correspondence between codon demand and tRNA-mediated anticodon composition during hematopoietic multilineage commitment and differentiation. Tri-modal profiling of mRNA, tRNA, and proteins from primary human T cells reveals tRNA-mediated regulation that partially explains the discordance between mRNA and protein levels, particularly for selenoproteins and transcription factors. Finally, we uncover a stress-responsive tRNA module defined by gene-internal promoter sequences. Together, our analyses resolve tRNAs as a previously undefined layer of translational control underlying cellular identity and cell-state transitions.

papers.title: Chromatin accessibility predictions reveal lineage-structured effects of noncoding variants across hematopoiesis
papers.abstract: Background. Noncoding variants account for over 90% of genome-wide association study (GWAS) findings, but their mechanisms are often unclear. Sequence-to-function models provide one approach to variant interpretation by predicting the effects of genetic variation on molecular phenotypes. ChromBPNet predicts variant effects on chromatin accessibility, but how these predictions are organized across differentiation hierarchies and relate to orthogonal predictions remains unclear. Results. We trained ChromBPNet models for 17 hematopoietic cell types and scored 302,830 variants. Of 242,307 variants accessible in at least one cell type, 5.6% were predicted to alter chromatin accessibility. Variants active in more cell types had larger predicted effects. Predicted effects also reflected hematopoietic lineage structure, with sharing declining with lineage distance while effect direction was preserved in 99.6% of parent-child comparisons. ChromBPNet predictions agreed with GWAS fine-mapping but largely identified distinct variants. Fine-mapping-only variants were enriched for coding and transcript-associated variation, whereas ChromBPNet-only variants were enriched for regulatory elements, accessible chromatin, and trait-relevant activity. In K562 CRISPRi datasets, predicted accessibility gain showed limited association with target-gene validation. Regulatory elements containing CTCF motifs were less likely to have validated target genes, consistent with a role in chromatin organization rather than gene activation. Conclusions. ChromBPNet and fine-mapping provide complementary information about variant function. Predicted accessibility effects identify the cell types in which noncoding variants are likely to act and capture relationships across the hematopoietic hierarchy, but provide limited information about the genes they regulate. All predictions are available at: https://bloodnnet.ccbr.utoronto.ca/.

papers.title: DeepRNAi: Predicting on- and off-target siRNA activity and establishing a benchmark
papers.abstract: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) silence target genes through RISC-mediated hybridization and cleavage, but can silence unintended transcripts and cause toxicity or complicate regulatory approval. In drug development, empirical assessment by qPCR and RNA-seq is slow, forces early candidate prioritization, and is limited by available species- and genome-appropriate cell models. While extensive empirical screening remains standard practice, there is a significant opportunity for modern AI methods to change this paradigm. We introduce DeepRNAi, a deep learning model that accurately predicts on- and off-target knockdown from siRNA and mRNA sequence. Trained on 16 million siRNA-transcript pairs from 2,031 siRNAs designed to interrogate known siRNA failure modes, and incorporating transcript context from biological foundation models, DeepRNAi is the first in silico method that approaches experimental accuracy. It generalizes across cell models, transcripts, genomes and species, and in a small study distinguishes approved therapeutics from hepatotoxic candidates. The value of DeepRNAi for prioritizing better candidates up front is supported by a genome-wide survey of 24.4 million siRNAs targeting 7,946 genes, which indicates that 90.1% of the 100 most potent siRNAs have at least some off-target concerns. To support the community, we are publishing a training and benchmark dataset containing 1.84 million siRNA-transcript pairs from 240 siRNAs.

papers.title: An oxidative mutational signature in normal tissues of a monoallelic MUTYH carrier
papers.abstract: Biallelic loss of MUTYH causes MUTYH-associated polyposis (OMIM: 608456), characterized by the oxidative base-excision-repair mutational signature SBS18, but whether the roughly 1 in 100 individuals who carry a single pathogenic MUTYH allele acquire a mutational phenotype in normal tissue is unknown. Analysis of multi-tissue sequencing of 25 donors from the Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network identified three heterozygous carriers of MUTYH p.Gly396Asp. One carrier showed SBS18 across multiple normal tissues, ranking first of 25 donors with three independent methods and remaining significant after adjustment for tissue, without a somatic, epigenetic or transcriptional second hit at the MUTYH locus. A single hypomorphic MUTYH allele can therefore leave a measurable oxidative mutational mark in healthy tissues, supporting tissue-level mutational readouts as an approach to cancer risk stratification within this common carrier state.

papers.title: Longitudinal miRNA-mRNA Profiling Reveals Network Reorganization in Preeclampsia
papers.abstract: Background: Preeclampsia (PE) is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity. Temporal dynamics of molecular dysregulation across pregnancy remain poorly understood. We performed longitudinal RNA sequencing of maternal whole blood to characterize miRNA-mRNA regulatory network evolution in PE. Methods: Whole-blood samples from early (M1: 10-18 weeks) and late pregnancy (M2: 32-38 weeks) were analyzed from 43 PE cases and 106 normotensive controls, including 109 paired samples (36 PE cases, 73 controls). Differential expression, temporal classification, pathway enrichment, and miRNA-mRNA network integration were performed. Placental expression support was assessed using internal RNA-seq and public databases. Key miRNA-mRNA interactions were experimentally validated in HTR-8/SVneo trophoblast cells. Results: PE exhibited marked temporal reorganization of miRNA-mRNA networks, with strongly opposing temporal effect sizes across overlapping miRNA and mRNA features (Spearman {rho} = -0.82, P < 0.0001). PI3K/AKT/mTORC1 signaling showed biphasic reversal (NES = +1.46, FDR = 0.028 at M1; NES = -1.64, FDR = 0.025 at M2), and heme-metabolism programs showed progressive suppression (2.1-fold NES intensification; FDR < 0.05 at both timepoints). Network analysis identified 29 high-confidence biphasic miRNA-mRNA pairs, including convergent targeting of ADGRA2 by three miRNAs and HSD17B1 by three miRNAs. miR-101-3p overexpression reduced DEPP1 mRNA (~40%) and protein (~26%) in trophoblast cells (P < 0.01), supporting a FOXO-DEPP1 axis. Blood-derived pairs showed pathway convergence with placental VGLL3-centered programs (PI3K/AKT, FOXO, TGF-{beta}, trophoblast differentiation). Conclusions: PE is associated with predominantly stage-specific or biphasic miRNA-mRNA network reorganization, with PI3K/AKT/mTORC1 dynamic remodeling and progressive heme-metabolism suppression. These findings support gestational-age-specific biomarker development and identify regulatory axes, including miR-101-3p [->] DEPP1, for mechanistic investigation.
